step: Apply for Certificate of Eligibility (COE) — employer files in Japan before employee visa application
authority: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (出入国在留管理庁)
form_name: Application for Certificate of Eligibility (在留資格認定証明書交付申請)
field_label: Certificate of Eligibility (在留資格認定証明書)
deadline_label: File at least 3 months before intended start date; COE valid for 3 months once issued
non_obvious_official_guidance: The employer or authorised representative in Japan submits the COE application to the nearest Regional Immigration Services Bureau or via the Immigration Bureau's e-Notification online system. Once issued, the COE is sent to the employee abroad to accompany their visa application at a Japanese embassy or consulate.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many HR teams assume the employee applies directly for a work visa. Japan's system requires the Japan-side employer to obtain the COE first — the employee cannot apply for it themselves. Processing takes 1–3 months with no guaranteed timeline; expedited processing does not exist. Missing this step can push a start date back by months. The COE expires 3 months after issue, so timing must be coordinated precisely.
non_obvious_action_required: Initiate the COE process at least 3–4 months before the intended start date. Japan-side HR or an immigration lawyer must file. Do not begin employee-side visa preparation until the COE is in hand. Monitor the 3-month COE validity window and ensure the employee enters Japan before it expires — a lapsed COE requires a new application from scratch.
source: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — Certificate of Eligibility Procedures

step: Determine correct status of residence (zairyu shikaku) category before COE application
authority: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (出入国在留管理庁)
form_name: N/A — internal determination before filing
field_label: Status of Residence Category (在留資格)
deadline_label: Determine before COE application — must be established before any immigration filing
non_obvious_official_guidance: Common work-related status categories include: Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services (技術・人文知識・国際業務), Intra-company Transferee (企業内転勤), Highly Skilled Professional (高度専門職), and Specified Skilled Worker (特定技能). Each has specific eligibility criteria covering education, work experience, and job duties.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Selecting the wrong status category is one of the leading causes of COE rejection. 'Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services' requires a documented connection between the employee's degree or 10-year work history and the Japan role — even an indirect link (e.g., economics degree for a software role) can qualify if clearly argued. 'Intra-company Transferee' requires 1+ year of continuous employment at the overseas entity. Mismatching category to actual on-the-ground duties is also an immigration violation after entry, not just a filing error.
non_obvious_action_required: Map the employee's academic background, work history, and actual Japan job description to the correct status category before COE filing. For intra-company transferees, verify and document 1+ year of tenure at the home entity. Engage a Japan immigration lawyer to review the category selection — a rejected COE wastes 1–3 months and cannot be expedited on resubmission.
source: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — Status of Residence Categories

step: Apply for Japan work visa at Japanese embassy or consulate in home country (after COE is in hand)
authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Japanese Embassy or Consulate in home country
form_name: Visa Application Form (査証申請書)
field_label: Japan Work Visa (就労ビザ)
deadline_label: After COE issuance; apply at least 2–4 weeks before intended travel date
source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Visa for Long-Term Stay

step: Check social security totalization agreement with home country and obtain Certificate of Coverage if applicable
authority: Japan Pension Service (日本年金機構) / Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare — bilateral social security agreement authority
form_name: Certificate of Coverage (適用証明書) — issued by home country social security authority
field_label: Totalization Agreement — Certificate of Coverage
deadline_label: Obtain Certificate of Coverage from home country before Japan arrival; provide to employer before shakai hoken enrollment is processed
responsible_party: employer (initiates) and employee (obtains certificate from home country authority)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Japan has social security totalization agreements with: Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Hungary, India, Italy, Netherlands, Philippines, Republic of Korea, Slovakia, Spain, Switzerland, United Kingdom, and United States (as of 2024). These agreements prevent dual social insurance contributions during assignments — the exempt period varies by agreement (typically up to 5 years).
non_obvious_actual_reality: Without a Certificate of Coverage, the employer must enrol the employee in shakai hoken (Japanese social insurance) regardless of contributions already being paid in the home country — resulting in simultaneous double contributions. Employees from countries with no totalization agreement (including many in Asia and Africa) face unavoidable double contributions which must be costed into the assignment budget. The Certificate of Coverage must be in the employer's hands before enrollment is filed; retroactive exemption is administratively difficult.
non_obvious_action_required: Before the employee departs, verify whether a totalization agreement exists between Japan and the home country. If yes, instruct the employee to apply for a Certificate of Coverage from the home country's social security authority (e.g., HMRC for UK nationals, SSA for US nationals, Deutsche Rentenversicherung for German nationals) — allow 4–8 weeks for processing. Provide it to Japan HR before the first payroll cycle. Retain it on file as the formal exemption justification.
source: Japan Pension Service — Status of Social Security Agreements

step: Conduct permanent establishment (PE) risk assessment for seconding entity before assignment begins
authority: National Tax Agency of Japan (国税庁) — applicable Japan bilateral tax treaty
form_name: N/A — internal tax-legal assessment; no filing unless PE is determined to exist
field_label: Permanent Establishment Risk (恒久的施設リスク — PE Risk)
deadline_label: Complete before secondment begins — PE risk arises from day 1 of activities
responsible_party: employer (home-country entity, with Japan tax adviser)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under Japan's bilateral tax treaties, a home-country entity may be deemed to have a permanent establishment (PE) in Japan where it maintains a fixed place of business or where a person habitually exercises authority to conclude contracts on its behalf. A PE subjects the home entity to Japanese corporate tax on profits attributable to that PE.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Japan's National Tax Agency significantly increased scrutiny of PE risks from seconded employees following BEPS implementation in 2018–2020. A secondee who retains decision-making authority for the home entity, negotiates or signs contracts in Japan on the home entity's behalf, or directs Japan-based operations on behalf of the home entity can trigger a PE finding. This is a corporate tax exposure for the sending company — not merely an individual payroll issue — and can result in substantial back-tax assessments.
non_obvious_action_required: Commission a PE risk analysis from a Japan tax adviser before the secondment begins. Review the secondment agreement to ensure: (a) the employee is under the management and control of the Japan host entity during the assignment; (b) the home entity does not exercise day-to-day direction over the secondee; (c) the employee does not sign contracts on behalf of the home entity from Japan. Document the control arrangement carefully and retain the secondment agreement.
source: National Tax Agency Japan — Permanent Establishment (English guidance)

step: Determine Japan tax residency status (resident / non-permanent resident / non-resident) and advise on non-permanent resident planning window
authority: National Tax Agency of Japan (国税庁) — Income Tax Act
form_name: N/A — status determined by facts of residence; relevant to withholding setup and year-end filing obligation
field_label: Japan Tax Residency Status (居住者 / 非永住者 / 非居住者)
deadline_label: Determine at commencement of Japan employment; reassess at 5-year residency mark when non-permanent resident status ends
responsible_party: employer (payroll and withholding setup) and employee (with Japan tax adviser)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under Japan's Income Tax Act: a 'resident' (居住者) has a domicile in Japan or has continuously resided in Japan for 1+ year and is taxable on worldwide income. A 'non-permanent resident' (非永住者) is a resident who is not a Japanese national and has been resident in Japan for 5 years or fewer in the past 10 years — taxable on Japan-source income and overseas income remitted to Japan, but not on overseas income retained abroad. A 'non-resident' is taxed only on Japan-source income.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The non-permanent resident (NPR) status is a significant — and widely unknown — tax advantage for foreign nationals in their first 5 years in Japan. During the NPR period, overseas income (bonuses paid offshore, RSUs vesting and held in a home-country account, dividends, rental income) is Japan-tax-free as long as it is NOT remitted to a Japan bank account. This creates a material planning window: offshore income retained abroad during the NPR period may be entirely exempt from Japan income tax. At the 5-year mark, NPR status ends automatically and worldwide income becomes fully taxable — often triggering a substantial increase in effective tax rate with no warning.
non_obvious_action_required: Brief the employee and payroll team on NPR status at onboarding. Advise the employee to avoid remitting large overseas income amounts to Japan bank accounts without first taking tax advice. Set a calendar reminder at the 5-year anniversary for both HR and the employee. For employees with RSUs, stock options, overseas rental income, or bonuses paid in the home country, engage a Japan tax adviser immediately — the NPR rules are complex and the planning window cannot be recovered once closed.
source: National Tax Agency Japan — Tax Guide for Foreigners (2023 edition)

step: Receive residence card (zairyu card) at designated port of entry immigration counter
authority: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — border control at designated port of entry
form_name: N/A — issued automatically at immigration counter for holders of a work visa valid over 3 months
field_label: Residence Card (在留カード — Zairyu Card)
deadline_label: At arrival; immediate issuance at designated airports only
non_obvious_official_guidance: Residence cards are issued at the immigration counter on arrival at the following designated airports only: Narita International, Tokyo Haneda, Kansai International, Chubu Centrair International, Fukuoka, New Chitose, and Hiroshima International. The card is issued on the spot to holders of a work visa valid for more than 3 months.
non_obvious_actual_reality: If the employee arrives through any non-designated port (smaller regional airports or seaports), the immigration stamp will read 'Residence Card to be Issued Later' (在留カード後日交付) and the card must be collected from the nearest Regional Immigration Services Bureau — a separate trip required within a few days of arrival. This is frequently missed: the employee arrives, clears customs, and assumes they are fully processed, not realising a follow-up government office visit is required. Without the zairyu card in hand, address registration and bank account opening cannot proceed.
non_obvious_action_required: Always route the employee's first entry into Japan through a designated airport — Narita, Haneda, or Kansai are most common. Confirm the routing before booking travel. If 'Residence Card to be Issued Later' is stamped, brief the employee immediately to visit the nearest Regional Immigration Services Bureau — bring the passport with the entry stamp. Do not proceed with address registration until the physical card is in hand.
source: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — Residence Card Information

step: Register residential address at municipal office (juminhyo — resident registration) within 14 days
authority: Municipal office (市区町村役場) — city hall, ward office, or town/village office
form_name: Notification of Moving In (転入届)
field_label: Resident Registration (住民登録 — Juminhyo)
deadline_label: Within 14 days of establishing the address in Japan
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals intending to reside in Japan for more than 3 months must register their address with the local municipal office within 14 days of moving in, as required by the Basic Resident Registration Act (住民基本台帳法). The zairyu card and passport are required. The address is recorded on the reverse of the zairyu card at the counter on the same day.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 14-day deadline is strict and widely unknown to newly arrived employees. Juminhyo registration triggers My Number assignment and is a hard prerequisite for virtually every subsequent administrative step: social insurance enrollment, My Number Card application, bank account opening, and resident tax. Without registration, the employee cannot be formally onboarded for shakai hoken or open a bank account at major institutions. Visiting the municipal office promptly in week 1 prevents cascading delays across all downstream steps.
non_obvious_action_required: Schedule the municipal office visit on day 2 or 3 of arrival — do not wait until day 14. Bring the zairyu card and passport. If the employee is initially in company-provided housing or a hotel, they can register the employer's address temporarily and update within 14 days of moving to their permanent address. Note that ward offices in major cities (e.g., Tokyo's 23 wards) have specific counter hours and some require appointments — check in advance and confirm the nearest office.
source: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications — Resident Registration Procedures for Foreign Nationals

step: Receive My Number (Individual Number) notification letter by registered post after juminhyo registration
authority: Municipal office / Digital Agency (デジタル庁) — Japan Individual Number system
form_name: My Number Initial Notification Letter (マイナンバー通知書)
field_label: My Number (個人番号 — 12-digit Individual Number)
deadline_label: Notification dispatched by registered post approximately 2–3 weeks after juminhyo registration; provide to employer promptly on receipt
non_obvious_official_guidance: Upon juminhyo registration the municipal office assigns a 12-digit My Number. An initial notification letter (マイナンバー通知書) is sent by registered post (書留郵便) to the registered address. The number must be provided to the employer for income tax withholding and social insurance enrollment filings.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The notification requires a recipient signature on delivery. If the employee is absent, the postal service holds it briefly before returning it to the municipal office — collection then requires a separate in-person visit with ID. Many newly arrived employees miss delivery because they are in temporary accommodation, the mailbox carries no name, or they are unaware a signed-for letter is coming at all. Late provision of the My Number delays the employer's shakai hoken and koyo hoken filing obligations.
non_obvious_action_required: Before registration: affix the employee's name to the mailbox at the registered address. Brief the employee that a registered letter requiring a signature will arrive within 3 weeks of registration — they must be available or arrange redelivery. If delivery is missed, collect in person at the municipal office with the zairyu card. Provide the number to HR the same day it is received. Plan simultaneously to apply for the My Number Card (IC card) as a separate step — the notification letter alone is not a photo ID.
source: Digital Agency Japan — My Number System Overview

step: Enroll employee in shakai hoken (employer social insurance: health insurance + employees' pension)
authority: Japan Pension Service (日本年金機構) / Health Insurance Society (健康保険組合) or Japan Health Insurance Association (全国健康保険協会)
form_name: Notification of Acquisition of Insured Status (被保険者資格取得届)
field_label: Shakai Hoken Enrollment (社会保険加入)
deadline_label: File within 5 days of employee start date (employer statutory obligation)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must file the Notification of Acquisition of Insured Status with the Japan Pension Service or the employer's Health Insurance Society within 5 days of the employee's start date. This simultaneously enrolls the employee in Employees' Health Insurance (健康保険) and Employees' Pension Insurance (厚生年金保険). Combined employer-plus-employee contribution rates are approximately 30% of standard monthly remuneration (verify current rates with the Japan Pension Service for the applicable year).
non_obvious_actual_reality: If a totalization agreement Certificate of Coverage is in effect, the employee is exempt from shakai hoken contributions — but the Certificate must be in the employer's hands before enrollment is processed; retroactive exemption is administratively difficult. For employees from non-agreement countries, double social security contributions are unavoidable and must be costed into the assignment budget. From late 2024, the traditional paper health insurance card (健康保険被保険者証) is being phased out and replaced by the My Number Card functioning as health insurance card (マイナ保険証) — confirm current transition status when enrolling.
non_obvious_action_required: Before filing: confirm whether a Certificate of Coverage applies. If exempt: retain the certificate, document the exemption, do not file enrollment. If not exempt: file within 5 days and factor the combined ~30% social insurance cost into total employment cost modelling. The employee's My Number is required on the form. Provide the employee with proof of insurance enrollment (and the health insurance card or My Number Card instructions) so they can access medical care immediately.
source: Japan Pension Service — Procedures for Enrollment of Insured Persons

step: Enroll in National Health Insurance (kokumin kenko hoken) — mandatory if not covered by employer shakai hoken
authority: Municipal office (市区町村) — National Health Insurance section
form_name: Application for National Health Insurance Enrollment (国民健康保険加入申請)
field_label: National Health Insurance (国民健康保険 — Kokumin Kenko Hoken)
deadline_label: Within 14 days of becoming a resident, or within 14 days of losing other health insurance coverage
source: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare — National Health Insurance Overview

step: Enroll in National Pension (kokumin nenkin) — mandatory if not covered by employer shakai hoken
authority: Japan Pension Service (日本年金機構) via municipal office
form_name: National Pension Category 1 Enrollment Application (国民年金被保険者関係届書)
field_label: National Pension (国民年金 — Kokumin Nenkin)
deadline_label: Within 14 days of becoming a resident or within 14 days of losing employees' pension coverage
source: Japan Pension Service — National Pension Enrollment

step: Apply for My Number Card (IC card) — serves as photo ID and is replacing the paper health insurance card
authority: Municipal office (市区町村) / Japan Agency for Local Authority Information Systems (J-LIS)
form_name: My Number Card Application (個人番号カード交付申請書)
field_label: My Number Card (マイナンバーカード)
deadline_label: No statutory deadline; apply as soon as My Number notification letter is received; card ready in approximately 4–6 weeks
non_obvious_official_guidance: The My Number Card is an IC card carrying the holder's photo, name, address, date of birth, gender, and My Number. It is issued free of charge by the municipal office upon application. A separate application is required — the My Number notification letter alone does not generate the card automatically.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The My Number Card is technically optional but has become practically essential. From late 2024 it functions as the health insurance card (マイナ保険証) as the traditional paper card is phased out. Major banks increasingly require it as primary photo ID for account opening. It enables e-Tax filing, online pension record access, and digital government services. Employees who do not apply in the first month face a 4–6 week processing gap that can block bank account opening and healthcare access at the precise moment they need both.
non_obvious_action_required: Apply at the municipal office as soon as the My Number notification letter arrives — bring the letter, zairyu card, and a passport-size photo (some offices photograph on-site). The completed card is collected at the counter approximately 4–6 weeks later; a second visit is required to set PINs. Brief the employee that until the card arrives, they must carry any paper health insurance card issued at shakai hoken enrollment and the notification letter as their My Number proof document.
source: Digital Agency Japan — My Number Card Application

step: Open Japanese bank account for salary receipt
authority: Bank or financial institution — regulated by Financial Services Agency (金融庁)
form_name: Account opening application (口座開設申込書) — varies by institution
field_label: Japan Bank Account
deadline_label: Open as soon as possible; salary must be paid by bank transfer under Labour Standards Act Article 24
non_obvious_official_guidance: Japan's Labour Standards Act requires salary to be paid directly to the employee, in principle by bank transfer to an account in the employee's name. Japanese banks require proof of identity (zairyu card or passport), proof of address (juminhyo certificate), and My Number for account opening by foreign nationals.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Major city banks (Mizuho, SMBC, MUFG) frequently decline newly arrived foreign nationals due to absence of Japan credit history, or require 6+ months of residence history before opening an account. Japan Post Bank (ゆうちょ銀行) and SBI Shinsei Bank are significantly more accessible to new residents and should be the first recommendation. Some bank branches require a personal seal (hanko/inkan) instead of a signature — entirely unknown to employees from Western countries; a basic 300-yen convenience-store stamp often suffices. Online banks (Rakuten Bank, PayPay Bank) require a Japanese SIM registered in the employee's own name, adding a prerequisite that must itself be addressed in week 1.
non_obvious_action_required: Pre-brief the employee before arrival: (1) register address day 1–2, obtain a juminhyo certificate; (2) direct them to Japan Post Bank or SBI Shinsei Bank as the most accessible first options; (3) warn them a hanko may be required at some branches. Arrange a Japan SIM card (registered in the employee's name) in week 1 if online banks are needed. Confirm with payroll whether the company has a preferred banking partner with a streamlined new-employee process, and establish a contingency for the first salary payment if the account is not yet open.
source: Financial Services Agency Japan — Financial Services for Foreign Residents

step: Enroll employee in employment insurance (koyo hoken) via Hello Work notification
authority: Hello Work (公共職業安定所 / ハローワーク) — Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
form_name: Employee Insurance Acquisition Notification (雇用保険被保険者資格取得届)
field_label: Employment Insurance (雇用保険 — Koyo Hoken)
deadline_label: Submit within 10 days of employee start date (employer statutory obligation)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must file the Employee Insurance Acquisition Notification with the nearest Hello Work office within 10 days of the employee's start date. Employment insurance applies to employees working 31+ hours per week and covers unemployment benefits, childcare leave benefits, and vocational training support.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Foreign nationals on work visas are fully entitled to — and must be enrolled in — employment insurance. It is not optional for the employer, and non-enrollment is a statutory violation. International companies with a small Japan presence frequently overlook this step, assuming it does not apply to foreign nationals. The enrollment requires the employee's My Number. The employment insurance card (雇用保険被保険者証) must be issued to the employee and retained — they will need it if they change employers or claim benefits.
non_obvious_action_required: Add koyo hoken enrollment to the Japan onboarding checklist alongside shakai hoken. File with the nearest Hello Work office within 10 days of the start date. Employee contribution is approximately 0.6% of wages; employer contribution approximately 0.95% (verify current FY rates). Issue the employment insurance certificate to the employee at onboarding and instruct them to keep it — it is not automatically reissued.
source: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare — Employment Insurance for Foreign Workers

step: Confirm workers' compensation insurance (rodo saigai hoken) coverage is active from employee's first day
authority: Labour Standards Inspection Office (労働基準監督署)
form_name: N/A — employer-level policy; verify active coverage at payroll setup
field_label: Workers' Compensation Insurance (労働者災害補償保険 — Rousai Hoken)
deadline_label: Must be active from the employee's first day of employment
source: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare — Workers' Compensation Insurance

step: Brief employee on resident tax (jumin-zei) first-year exemption and second-year billing shock
authority: Municipal tax office (市区町村 — 税務課 / 市民税課)
form_name: N/A — no filing required in year 1; resident tax notice issued automatically from June of year 2
field_label: Resident Tax (住民税 — Jumin-zei)
deadline_label: No payment due in year 1 of arrival; resident tax assessed and deducted from June of the following calendar year onward
non_obvious_official_guidance: Resident tax (住民税) is assessed at approximately 10% of prior-year taxable income and levied on individuals registered in Japan (juminhyo) as of January 1st of a given year. Payment is either via special collection (特別徴収 — monthly payroll deduction by employer) or ordinary collection (普通徴収 — 4 self-paid instalments). The June–May collection cycle means the first deductions begin in June.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Employees arriving after January 1st owe no resident tax in their first calendar year because they were not registered on January 1st. Payslips appear clean — no jumin-zei line — until June of year 2, when two months' worth are collected together in June and July, followed by monthly deductions thereafter. This produces a sudden effective pay cut of roughly JPY 200,000–400,000 per year split into monthly bites that employees experience as a shock if not warned. For tax-equalized secondees the employer must include year-2 resident tax in gross-up calculations — a planning gap many global mobility teams miss entirely.
non_obvious_action_required: At onboarding, tell the employee explicitly: 'You will not see resident tax on your payslip this year. From June next year, it will appear and is based on your income this year.' For tax-equalized assignees, ensure home HR/payroll includes resident tax in equalization modelling from year 2. Alert any employee departing Japan mid-year that they may still receive a resident tax bill for the prior year — often paid via ordinary collection after departure.
source: Tokyo Metropolitan Government — Guide to Resident Tax for Foreign Residents

step: Employee submits withholding exemption declaration to employer for income tax withholding setup
authority: National Tax Agency of Japan (国税庁)
form_name: Employee's Withholding Exemption Declaration (給与所得者の扶養控除等(異動)申告書)
field_label: Income Tax Withholding Declaration
deadline_label: Submit to employer before the first salary payment; annually by January for existing employees
responsible_party: employee (submits form to employer) / employer (withholds monthly and remits to tax office)
source: National Tax Agency Japan — Withholding Tax on Employment Income

step: Renew status of residence and residence card before expiry
authority: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — Regional Immigration Services Bureau
form_name: Application for Extension of Period of Stay (在留期間更新許可申請)
field_label: Status of Residence Renewal (在留期間更新)
deadline_label: Apply within 3 months before current status of residence expires; never allow expiry to lapse
non_obvious_official_guidance: Applications for extension of period of stay must be filed before the current status expires at the competent Regional Immigration Services Bureau. If filed before expiry, a special provision allows the employee to continue residing and working while the application is pending; an interim stamp is available on request.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many employees — and their HR teams — lose track of the zairyu card expiry date, which is identical to the status of residence expiry. Residing or working in Japan after expiry is a criminal offence under the Immigration Control Act, not merely an administrative lapse. Initial work status grants are frequently only 1 year even for experienced hires; 3-year and 5-year grants typically come at renewal. HR must maintain a live calendar of every employee's expiry date.
non_obvious_action_required: Record the residence card expiry date in HR systems at onboarding and set a 90-day advance alert. Applications must be filed at the Regional Immigration Services Bureau for the employee's prefecture of residence — confirm the correct office, as jurisdiction is by residence not by workplace. Online applications are available for some categories via the ISA e-Application system. Engage an immigration lawyer for renewal if there have been any role, salary, or employer-entity changes since the last grant.
source: Immigration Services Agency — Extension of Period of Stay Procedures

step: Complete annual year-end tax adjustment (nenmatsu chosei) with employer
authority: National Tax Agency of Japan (国税庁) — employer performs reconciliation
form_name: Withholding Exemption Declaration (給与所得者の扶養控除等(異動)申告書) plus Insurance Premium Deduction Declaration (給与所得者の保険料控除申告書)
field_label: Year-End Tax Adjustment (年末調整 — Nenmatsu Chosei)
deadline_label: Employee submits forms to employer by late November; employer reconciles and remits by January 20 of the following year
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers in Japan must perform an annual year-end tax adjustment reconciling income tax withheld throughout the year against the employee's actual tax liability, taking into account declared deductions (dependants, life insurance premiums, housing loan deductions, etc.). For most Japanese employees with a single employer this process functions as their annual income tax return.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Internationally mobile employees and secondees are frequently ineligible for the year-end adjustment alone and must also file a final income tax return (確定申告 — kakutei shinkoku) by March 15. This applies to any employee with: (a) overseas income, (b) RSUs or stock options vesting during the year, (c) annual Japan income exceeding JPY 20 million, or (d) income not subject to employer withholding. Many international companies process only the year-end adjustment and fail to flag the separate individual filing obligation — resulting in underpayment and penalties.
non_obvious_action_required: At the start of each calendar year, identify which employees require a kakutei shinkoku in addition to the year-end adjustment. Flag any employee with overseas income, RSUs/stock options, or split-salary arrangements. Provide those employees with a Japan tax adviser referral. Process the employer-side year-end adjustment correctly for all employees as the baseline even where individual filing is also required.
source: National Tax Agency Japan — Year-End Tax Adjustment (English)

step: File annual income tax return (kakutei shinkoku) — mandatory where overseas income, RSUs, or complex situations apply
authority: National Tax Agency of Japan (国税庁) — via e-Tax or district tax office
form_name: Final Return Form (確定申告書 — Form A or B, or e-Tax electronic submission)
field_label: Annual Income Tax Return (確定申告 — Kakutei Shinkoku)
deadline_label: February 16 – March 15 of the year following the tax year (e.g., March 15, 2025 for 2024 income)
responsible_party: employee (with tax adviser for cross-border cases)
source: National Tax Agency Japan — Final Return Filing (English)

step: Annual social insurance standard monthly remuneration review (santei kijo) — employer files each July
authority: Japan Pension Service (日本年金機構) / Health Insurance Society (健康保険組合)
form_name: Report on Wage Calculation Base Month (算定基礎届)
field_label: Standard Monthly Remuneration Annual Review (標準報酬月額の定時決定 — Santei Kijo)
deadline_label: Employer submits by July 10 each year; revised standard monthly remuneration applies October through the following September
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must submit the Wage Calculation Base Month Report (算定基礎届) to the Japan Pension Service each July, based on actual remuneration paid in April, May, and June. The revised Standard Monthly Remuneration (標準報酬月額) derived from this report determines social insurance contribution amounts for October through the following September.
non_obvious_actual_reality: For internationally mobile employees with split-salary arrangements, overseas allowances, or variable compensation, determining the correct 'remuneration' base is complex. Japan's rules include regular cash payments from the Japan entity and some employer-reimbursed overseas allowances; they exclude bonuses (handled separately via 賞与支払届), one-time payments, and severance. Underdeclaration leads to penalties and employee benefit shortfalls; overdeclaration increases costs unnecessarily. A mid-year revision (月額変更届 — gekkan henko todoke) is also required if remuneration shifts by 2+ standard monthly remuneration bands for 3 consecutive months — a commonly missed obligation.
non_obvious_action_required: Before the July filing, review all internationally mobile employees' remuneration components with a Japan social insurance adviser. Confirm which overseas allowances are includable. Check for any mid-year promotions or allowance changes that may have triggered a monthly revision obligation — file retroactively if missed. Maintain a record of each employee's Standard Monthly Remuneration for payslip reconciliation and cost modelling.
source: Japan Pension Service — Regular Determination of Standard Monthly Remuneration

step: Notify municipal office of address change and update zairyu card reverse within 14 days of moving
authority: Municipal office (旧・新市区町村役場) — Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
form_name: Moving-out notification (転出届) at old address + Moving-in notification (転入届) at new address; or 転居届 for moves within the same municipality
field_label: Address Change Registration
deadline_label: Within 14 days of moving to the new address
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals must notify their municipal office of any address change within 14 days. For cross-municipality moves: file 転出届 at the old office (may be filed up to 14 days before moving), then file 転入届 at the new office within 14 days of arrival. The new address is printed on the zairyu card reverse at the new office counter on the same day. Since 2012, updating the address at the municipal office simultaneously notifies immigration — no separate visit to the immigration bureau is required.
non_obvious_actual_reality: For moves between different cities or prefectures, failing to file the 転出届 at the old municipal office first is a common error — the new office cannot process the 転入届 without the 転出証明書 issued by the old office. Additionally, resident tax is levied by the municipality of residence as of January 1st each year — a mid-year address change does not shift the current year's tax liability, but the employer must update the payroll system's municipality record so the following year's special collection goes to the correct local authority.
non_obvious_action_required: When an employee moves between municipalities: (1) file 転出届 at the old office and obtain the 転出証明書; (2) file 転入届 at the new office within 14 days of moving and have the zairyu card address updated on the spot. Update HR and payroll records with the new municipality for resident tax purposes effective January 1st of the following year. For January 1st moves specifically, confirm with a tax adviser which municipality is entitled to that year's resident tax.
source: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications — Moving Procedures for Foreign Nationals

step: Claim pension lump-sum withdrawal payment (dattai ichiji kin) upon permanent departure from Japan
authority: Japan Pension Service (日本年金機構)
form_name: Application for Lump-sum Withdrawal Payments (脱退一時金請求書)
field_label: Pension Lump-Sum Withdrawal (脱退一時金 — Dattai Ichiji Kin)
deadline_label: File within 2 years of departure from Japan and loss of insured status; application can be submitted from overseas
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals enrolled in Japan's pension system for 6 months or more may apply for a lump-sum withdrawal of a portion of contributions within 2 years of permanently leaving Japan and losing insured status. The refund is subject to 20.42% withholding tax deducted in Japan before payment.
non_obvious_actual_reality: This entitlement is one of the most frequently missed financial benefits for departing foreign employees — the refund can be worth several hundred thousand yen. The 20.42% withholding tax can often be partially or fully reclaimed via a non-resident tax return filed by an appointed tax representative in Japan, depending on the applicable tax treaty. Critically, employees from totalization-agreement countries face an irrevocable binary choice: (a) claim the lump-sum withdrawal, forfeiting the right to count Japan pension years toward home-country entitlement, or (b) forgo the withdrawal and count those years under the totalization agreement toward home-country pension. The long-term financial value of each option depends on the employee's career trajectory and home-country pension rules — getting this wrong cannot be undone.
non_obvious_action_required: Brief every departing employee on the lump-sum withdrawal entitlement and its 2-year deadline before they leave Japan. If a totalization agreement applies, the employee must choose between withdrawal and totalization credit — engage a Japan pension or tax adviser to model both options before departure. Appoint a 納税管理人 (tax representative) in Japan before departure to handle the withholding tax refund filing. The application form is available from the Japan Pension Service and can be submitted from overseas by post.
source: Japan Pension Service — Lump-sum Withdrawal Payments for Foreign Nationals
